findings.title: The `rounds:M4.8b1` argument misattributes the rounds; .harness/review contradicts it, and in the flattering direction
findings.detail:
baselines/review.txt, the added `rounds:M4.8b1` line. Two claims, both false against the harness record.

CLAIM A: 'The filter itself -- one predicate applied at two listing sites -- passed both roles in round 1 with no finding against its logic, and every round since was spent on text ABOUT it.'
CLAIM B: 'Round 2 was the one that earned its keep: both reviewers independently measured `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))` as a surviving mutant.'

Measured, not argued. The three prior rounds are, by mtime in .harness/review: fcf8d15b8ee8 (reviewer 10:53, test-reviewer 10:57) = round 1; 006aa9aad9dd (11:08, 11:10) = round 2; 19d8ae11daa3 (11:19, 11:20) = round 3.

Round 1 -- fcf8d15b -- reviewer finding 1 is titled 'The round-trip equality -- the line the whole design argument rests on -- is not pinned by any test' and its body reads 'Surviving mutation, measured rather than argued: replace `return key.equals(keyFor(sequence));` with `return true;` and the entire sequencer module stays green'. Round 1 test-reviewer finding 1 is titled 'SURVIVING MUTANT, MEASURED: the canonical-regeneration half of isEntryKey is unconstrained by any test'. So the survivor Claim B dates to round 2 was measured by BOTH roles in ROUND 1 -- which is also what makes Claim A false, since that is a finding against the very half of the predicate the row calls the point of the design, and it is what produced LogKeysTest, the largest new test file in this diff.

Round 1 also carried two further findings against the PRODUCTION diff, not against text about it: reviewer finding 2, 'CommitLog.isEntryKey is a delegate with no caller anywhere in the tree', and test-reviewer finding 2, 'New method CommitLog.isEntryKey has no caller and no test; a no-op mutation kills nothing'. That is the deletion this commit performs.

And 'every round since was spent on text ABOUT it' / 'Everything after was successive drafts of ONE javadoc paragraph' is false for rounds 2 and 3 as well: round 2's test-reviewer measured 'Two mutations survive the whole suite: deleting either half of the guard in isEntryKey', and round 3's measured that the guards were 'pinned against DELETION but not against being narrowed to a proper prefix'. Each produced a new assertion in LogKeysTest, both of which I re-measured as killing today. The staged backlog-done.md row states this correctly ('A SECOND ROUND OF MUTATION FOUND THE TWO LENGTH GUARDS UNPINNED'; 'A FURTHER ROUND FOUND THEM PINNED AGAINST DELETION BUT NOT NARROWING'), so the two documents in this same commit contradict each other about the same rounds.

FAILURE SCENARIO: baselines/review.txt is the durable record a later session reads to decide whether an over-cap task was justified and what review is worth. This entry tells that reader that four rounds bought one corrected javadoc paragraph and that the reviewers found nothing in the code -- when the record shows three separately measured surviving mutants in the author's own predicate, one per round, each closed by a new assertion. Under review.md `two-round-cap` this line is the argument that buys rounds 3 and 4; an argument whose factual claims are refuted by the artifacts it describes suppresses the finding rather than recording it, which is exactly what rule `fixed-or-argued` exists to prevent. The error direction is not neutral: it exonerates the change and indicts only the prose.

REMEDY, and deliberately a small one: correct the two sentences to say that round 1 measured the round-trip survivor (both roles) and also removed the uncalled `CommitLog.isEntryKey`, that rounds 2 and 3 each measured a further guard mutant and added the assertion that kills it, and that what the rounds did NOT converge on was one javadoc paragraph. No code, test, red record or measurement changes. Do not restate a round count anywhere else in the entry -- the entry's own 'NO COUNT IS GIVEN HERE' remedy is right and should stay.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session reads baselines/review.txt to judge whether M4.8b1's four rounds were justified and what review bought. This entry tells it that the reviewers found nothing in the code and that rounds 2-4 were the author correcting one javadoc paragraph. .harness/review shows three separately measured surviving mutants in the author's own predicate -- the round-trip equality in round 1 (both roles), the two length-guard deletions in round 2, the startsWith narrowing in round 3 -- each closed by an assertion in LogKeysTest, and round 1 also removed an uncalled CommitLog.isEntryKey. Under review.md rule two-round-cap this line is what buys rounds 3 and 4, so a false account of what the rounds found suppresses those findings while leaving a record that looks like disclosure -- the same shape as the false equivalence arguments M4.8a's own entry records shipping in baselines/mutants.txt. It also contradicts this commit's own backlog-done.md row, which describes rounds 2 and 3 correctly.

findings.title: The new `bins.delta` comment gives a false reason for why the two cases above miss the narrowing mutant
findings.detail:
sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LogKeysTest.java, the comment added this round: 'The two cases above miss it, since neither starts with `bins` either.'

`KEYS` is `new LogKeys("bins", 1)`, so `KEYS.logPrefix()` is `bins/ctl/log/0/0000000000000001/` -- which starts with `bins`. The second case above is `KEYS.isEntryKey(KEYS.logPrefix() + "x")`, and that key therefore DOES start with `bins`. It misses the narrowing mutant for a different reason: it fails `endsWith(SUFFIX)` and returns false before any slicing. Only the first case, `".delta"`, misses it for the reason given.

The conclusion is right and the assertion is right -- I measured that `startsWith(logPrefix)` narrowed to `startsWith(prefix)` fails only aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing, and that it fails on the `bins.delta` case -- and the `.as()` descriptions on the two older assertions are correct. It is the parenthetical justification that is false.

FAILURE SCENARIO: not behavioural. The next reader reasons from this sentence that a key under the log prefix does not start with the bare prefix component, which is the opposite of true and is the exact confusion the `bins.delta` case exists to expose. Per review.md `minors-land` this lands; fixing it is permitted and, given the history of this task, arguably the wrong call -- if it is fixed, 'since only the first starts with neither, and the second fails the suffix guard first' is the accurate form.

Separately, and not a finding: the paragraph's 'REACHABLE TODAY' banner is exact for the endsWith guard, whose instance `<logPrefix>x` a LIST really can return, and looser for the startsWith guard, since every key today's LIST returns starts with the log prefix by construction. The banner names the reachable instance, so it does not overstate in the way the earlier draft did.
findings.failure_scenario: Not behavioural: the assertion is correct and I measured it killing the startsWith(prefix) narrowing mutant. The next reader of LogKeysTest reasons from 'neither starts with bins either' that a key under the log prefix does not start with the bare prefix component -- the opposite of true, since logPrefix() is built as prefix + "/ctl/log/0/..." -- and can then delete or weaken the bins.delta case believing one of the older assertions already covers the operand. It does not: KEYS.logPrefix() + "x" starts with bins and misses the mutant only because it fails the endsWith guard first.
